content.title: Extracted recommendations (page)

points: Diltiazem or verapamil are not recommended in patients with HFrEF due to risk of HF worsening and HF hospitalization.
NSAIDs or COX-2 inhibitors are not recommended in patients with HF as they increase the risk of HF worsening and HF hospitalization.
The DPP-4 inhibitor saxagliptin is not recommended in patients with HF.
Aortic valve intervention (TAVI or SAVR) is recommended in patients with HF and severe high-gradient aortic stenosis to reduce mortality and improve symptoms.
Choice between TAVI and SAVR should be made by the Heart Team, considering patient preference, age, surgical risk, clinical/anatomical/procedural aspects.

SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM at risk of cardiovascular events to reduce hospitalizations for HF, major CV events, end-stage renal dysfunction, and CV death.
SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM and HFrEF to reduce hospitalizations for HF and CV death.
Thiazolidinediones (glitazones) are not recommended in patients with HF because they increase risk of HF worsening and hospitalization.
All patients with HF should be periodically screened for anaemia and iron deficiency with full blood count, serum ferritin concentration, and TSAT.
Treatment of anaemia in HF with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents is not recommended in the absence of other indications for this therapy.
Adaptive servo-ventilation is not recommended in patients with HFrEF and predominant central sleep apnoea because of increased all-cause and CV mortality.
Cancer patients at increased risk for cardiotoxicity should have CV evaluation before scheduled anticancer therapy, preferably by a cardiologist with cardio-oncology experience.

Tafamidis is recommended in patients with genetically proven hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (hATTR-CA) and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms, CV hospitalization and mortality.
Tafamidis is recommended in patients with wild-type transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (wtTTR-CA) and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms, CV hospitalization and mortality.
